text:
todd: Hey team – customer hitting 400 on tool invoke (function call). They get a schema validation error and can't progress. Customer: AcmePayments. Request ID: req_7e2f9a33. Error says additionalProperties and missing required fields. Sending payload + error below.

maria: sorry that's blocking, we'll triage. Can you paste the exact error body and the payload you sent? also which model+version and environment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

(todd pasted) todd: payload we sent:
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"submit_charge\",
  \"args\": {
    \"amount\": 1200,
    \"currency\": \"usd\",
    \"user_id\": 12345,
    \"billing_profile\": { \"plan\": \"enterprise\" }
  }
}
```
response body:
```json
{
  \"error\": \"schema_validation_failed\",
  \"details\": [
    {\"path\": \"/args/session_id\", \"message\": \"required property missing\"},
    {\"path\": \"/args/user_id\", \"message\": \"expected string, got integer\"},
    {\"path\": \"/args/billing_profile\", \"message\": \"additionalProperties not allowed\"}
  ],
  \"request_id\": \"req_7e2f9a33\"
}
```

maria: thanks. model: gpt-open-2.1 (hosted). quick notes: 1) the function schema for submit_charge expects user_id as string, session_id required, disallows additionalProperties (so billing_profile is not permitted). 2) Are they using Redwood SDK or calling our raw /invoke API?

(todd) todd: raw /v1/invoke - they're doing server-to-server from a lambda. Auth token is valid (they passed 200 status on other endpoints). Latency wasn't the issue, this is immediate 400.

maria: OK. can you repro locally and attach curl? also include full request headers (redact tokens). If it's raw invoke we should show customer how to coerce types and remove extra fields or update function schema.

(todd) todd: repro curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"tool\":\"submit_charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":1200,\"currency\":\"usd\",\"user_id\":12345,\"billing_profile\":{\"plan\":\"enterprise\"}}}'
```

maria: forwarding to eng. @jay can you weigh in on whether the model metadata/func schema was recently changed? also if we can relax validation server-side or provide a nicer error mapping.

(jay) jay: looking. quick check: function schema in model registry for submit_charge currently:
```json
{
  \"name\": \"submit_charge\",
  \"parameters\": {
    \"type\": \"object\",
    \"properties\": {
      \"user_id\": {\"type\":\"string\"},
      \"amount\": {\"type\":\"number\"},
      \"currency\": {\"type\":\"string\"},
      \"session_id\": {\"type\":\"string\"}
    },
    \"required\": [\"session_id\",\"user_id\",\"amount\",\"currency\"],
    \"additionalProperties\": false
  }
}
```
This matches the error. Newer client libs used to coerce ints -> strings for user_id; raw invoke does not. Also billing_profile not part of schema so it gets rejected.

(jay) jay: options: 1) short-term support workaround: have customer strip billing_profile and stringify user_id and provide session_id (they can generate a UUID). 2) medium: we could add a server-side shim on raw invoke to coerce simple primitives (int->string) and drop unknown properties for function calls for hosted tenants — but that's a behavior change and could hide issues. 3) long-term: update docs + SDK to clearly enforce function schemas client-side and include better error messages.

maria: customer prefers solution 1 for now. todd: can you try sending session_id and user_id as string? and confirm if billing_profile can be excluded or must be sent (they said they need plan metadata downstream).

(todd) todd: they need billing_profile. if we drop it, downstream reconciliation fails. Is there an alternate field to attach metadata?

(jay) jay: two quick paths: a) we ask them to put billing_profile inside a top-level metadata header in their request (we can add a custom X-Redwood-Meta header or use the top-level `metadata` arg if the tool schema allows it). b) if billing_profile is required by their business logic inside the function, we need to update the function schema in the model registry to accept billing_profile (and its structure) and then deploy a new model version. That requires product sign-off and follow-up.

maria: I'm going to open a support ticket and label as escalation -> eng-required. todd: please try the quick workaround (stringify user_id and attach session_id) and confirm whether billing_profile can be supplied via metadata header as a temporary route. I'll also ask product whether we can fast-track a schema update for this model.

(sre-bot): Incident created: SUP-3421 | priority: P2 | assigned: eng -> jay | link: https://redwood.app/incidents/SUP-3421

(todd) todd: tried the workaround, now payload:
```json
{\"tool\":\"submit_charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":1200,\"currency\":\"usd\",\"user_id\":\"12345\",\"session_id\":\"s_9b8c7d6e\"},\"metadata\":{\"billing_profile\":{\"plan\":\"enterprise\"}}}
```
response: 200 OK, returns {\"status\":\"queued\",\"charge_id\":\"chg_0042\"}

maria: great — closing immediate customer blocker. tagging for follow-up: 1) jay to propose schema change timeline, 2) docs/SDK doc for validation + examples, 3) consider safer server-side lenience toggle for hosted tenants.

(jay) jay: I'll add a short RFC and link it to SUP-3421, ETA EOW for proposal. If product approves quick model version bump, we can roll within 2 sprints.

maria: thanks everyone. todd: I'll send the customer the workaround + recommended remediation plan now. :white_check_mark:
